evidence.field: PDF p. 77, printed p. 65; 尔 entry; original scan visually inspected
evidence.text: The entry says 尔 is the simplified form of 爾; the construction of early 爾 forms is unclear; and bronze inscriptions use 尔 as a second-person pronoun. It reports examples from the Warring States Zhongshan Wang Ding and describes graphic developments of 尔. This concerns 尔 and does not analyze the formation of 你. I inspected the complete 尔 entry and its glyph sequence in the scan; the OCR excerpt agrees with the visible prose for the claims used.
evidence.title: 字源, 2012, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社 / 辽宁人民出版社, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.text: The entry identifies 你 as a singular second-person pronoun, absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and Shuowen. It cites 集韻·止韻 “你，汝也,” 隋書·李密傳, and later usage. The cited wording does not independently establish the date of its textual witness.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭 你

evidence.field: 你; 說文釋形、字樣說明、釋義
evidence.text: The entry says 你 is not recorded in Shuowen, describes the right side as 尔, and cites 集韻’s gloss “你，乃里切。汝也” and a second-person example from 周書. It also lists plural, possessive, and generic uses from later texts, without establishing a dated semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 你

evidence.text: The entry describes 尔 (anciently 尒) as taking the upper part of 爾, and reports its use for second-person forms including ‘you/your’; it cites a Warring States inscription and manuscript examples. It says 尔 later developed into modern 你. This supports a reported lexical/graphic relationship, not a phonetic role for 尔 within 你.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 字頭 尔

evidence.text: The 爾 entry indexes 尔 as an alternative form and explicitly says contemporary 尔 is the simplified character for 爾. This establishes 爾 → 尔 as standard simplification, not a component-origin claim for 你.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》— 爾

evidence.text: The official record identifies 你 as U+4F60. The opened record supports contemporary character metadata; it did not provide legible retrieved text in this inspection to confirm the IDS or reading asserted in prior research.

gaps: No inspected source directly demonstrates the formation of 你 as 亻 + phonetic 尔, or establishes the competing 人 + 尔 ideographic proposal. Keep the formation disputed/plausible rather than settled.
[SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 字源 PDF p. 1100, supplied OCR spans [glyph:p001]–[glyph:p009] in 女/姓 material: this is unrelated to the 你 headword and was not inspected; do not use as evidence about 你.

The corpus search did not establish a 你 headword passage; the inspected 字源 page is PDF p. 77 (printed p. 65), the 尔 component entry. The earlier supplied 你 candidate at PDF p. 1100 is a locator mention, not a verified 你 entry.
Exact earliest surviving written attestation of 你 and the transmission date of quoted 隋書 wording remain unresolved. Dictionary-cited examples do not alone establish witness chronology.
MOE lists plural, possessive, and generic uses but does not date their development or establish semantic links from singular ‘you’.

A matched 你–尔 reading comparison in a single historical reconstruction system was not verified. The required Unicode pages for U+4F60 and U+5C14 were inaccessible; local HSK extract rows provide modern metadata only.
